clue.text: Wild child with playmate rejects daughter with great force

indicators.note: wild things are out of control, so the letters that follow are thrown into a new order
to reject is to throw out, so one letter is taken out of the pooled words

parts.note: D is the standard abbreviation for daughter in family trees

explanation.surface: An unruly child and a friend shove a girl away with real vigour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rejects' takes D out of CHILD PLAYMATE, leaving CHILPLAYMATE, and 'Wild' shuffles those twelve letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something emphatically means doing it forcefully and insistently, so the adverb phrase is a synonym.

clue.text: Plague occurring where old city river enters sea

indicators.note: one piece entering another means it goes inside it, so the city and river sit within the sea word

parts.note: the main is an old poetic word for the open sea
Ur is the ancient city of Mesopotamia, the crossword's favourite old city
R is the standard abbreviation for river on maps

explanation.surface: An outbreak of disease where an ancient city's river runs into the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'enters' is the container signal; 'sea' as main is old poetic usage, as in the Spanish Main.
explanation.definitionFit: Murrain is an archaic word for an infectious disease of cattle, and more loosely any pestilence.

clue.text: Worker takes deliveries after transfer

parts.note: a hand is a manual labourer, as in farmhand
in cricket an over is a set of six balls bowled, or deliveries

explanation.surface: A labourer picks up some parcels once a job move has gone through.
explanation.walkthrough: 'deliveries' is cricket: an over is six balls bowled by one bowler. 'takes' and 'after' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: A handover is the passing of control or responsibility from one party to another.

clue.text: Main event, reportedly, ended in dead heat

indicators.note: something reported is passed on by word of mouth, so the sound of the phrase is meant, not its spelling

parts.note: the main is the sea, and the tide is its regular rise and fall

explanation.surface: The headline bout, so the reports say, finished level.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main event' looks like the top fight on a card, but 'main' means the sea, whose event is the tide.
explanation.definitionFit: Competitors who tie finish level, which is exactly what a dead heat is.

clue.text: Study decided press chief was confused

parts.note: to con is an old verb meaning to study or learn by heart
a court that found for one side decided in its favour
an editor heads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A newspaper boss's mind was made up after reviewing the case, and yet they were muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'was' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: To be confounded is to be bewildered or perplexed, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Turner's European articles

parts.note: la is the feminine definite article in French, Italian and Spanish
the is the English definite article, English being a European language

explanation.surface: Items about the English painter Turner from European writers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turner's' suggests the painter J M W Turner, but it means a woodturner's tool; 'European articles' supplies two words for 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: A woodturner shapes timber on a rotating machine, so this tool is the turner's own.

clue.text: Pined for the old composer, deceased

parts.note: ye is an archaic spelling of the
Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
D is the abbreviation for died or deceased in records

explanation.surface: Someone longed for the long-dead composer of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word; Thomas Arne is an 18th-century English composer.
explanation.definitionFit: To yearn is to long wistfully for something, which is what pining means.

clue.text: After a swim duck established offspring's energy reserves

parts.note: a dip is a quick swim
a duck in cricket is a score of nothing, written O
something set is fixed or settled
issue means children or descendants, the possessive being dropped

explanation.surface: Having had a bathe, a waterbird's established young lay down their fat stores.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricket score of nought, O. 'After' is a link word here.
explanation.definitionFit: Body fat is the store of energy the body draws on, and this is its anatomical name.

clue.text: Bar promoting pleasant atmosphere?

parts.note: read as a pub or club with a good ambience, but the bar is a cake for washing, and the pleasant atmosphere is air free of body odour

explanation.surface: A pub that aims for a nice ambience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bar' wants to be a pub; it is a bar of something used in the shower.
explanation.definitionFit: A soap with an added antiperspirant agent keeps the user smelling fresh, improving the air around them.

clue.text: Restraint of the French organised church

parts.note: du is French for of the
to run something is to organise it, giving ran
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A controlled French congregation keeps its members in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organised' looks like an anagram signal, but it gives RAN (ran a business).
explanation.definitionFit: Durance is an archaic word for imprisonment or confinement, a form of restraint.

clue.text: Small egg republican consumed with salt

parts.note: a nit is the egg of a louse
R stands for Republican in US politics
to consume food is to eat it, giving ate

explanation.surface: A Republican polishes off a tiny egg with a sprinkling of salt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Chemically a nitrate is a salt of nitric acid, such as saltpetre.

clue.text: Picture house publicist takes trouble

parts.note: PR, public relations, stands for a publicist's work
ado means fuss or bother

explanation.surface: A cinema's press officer runs into difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Picture house' suggests a cinema, but here it is a gallery full of pictures, Madrid's famous art museum.
explanation.definitionFit: Madrid's national art museum houses paintings by Velázquez and Goya, literally a home for pictures.

clue.text: Olympian takes writer under control

indicators.note: a word that takes another in holds it inside itself, so the writer goes within the god

parts.note: the Olympians were the Greek gods who lived on Mount Olympus
Jules Verne wrote Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea

explanation.surface: An Olympic athlete brings a novelist under their command.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Olympian' suggests a modern athlete; it is a god of Mount Olympus.
explanation.definitionFit: Something governed is ruled or regulated, which is to be held in check.

clue.text: Being this can cause old American to carry much weight

definitions.text: Being this can cause old American to carry much weight

parts.note: a glut is an excess, a great deal of something
a ton is a unit of weight
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: Overeating can make an elderly American carry a lot of extra pounds.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the result of greed, while its last words build the answer piece by piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Overeating habitually leads to weight gain, so a greedy eater may end up heavy.

clue.text: Northern town gives light to the German nation

parts.note: the sun is the source of daylight
der is the masculine form of the in German
a land is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A northern English town lends illumination to Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: SUNDERLAND is a city in north-east England, on the River Wear. 'gives' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sunderland is a city in Tyne and Wear in the north-east of England.

clue.text: Flower's fragrance, we hear

definitions.note: a flower is something that flows, a river; the 's stands for is

indicators.note: hearing points to how a word sounds when spoken rather than how it is spelt

parts.note: an odour is a scent or smell

explanation.surface: The scent of a bloom, so people say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flower' reads as a bloom but means flow-er, a river: the Oder runs between Germany and Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: In crosswords a flower is a river, something that flows, and the Oder is a central European river.

clue.text: General set up places in Indian city

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it, so the turned places go within the city

parts.note: Agra is the Indian city of the Taj Mahal

indicators.note: in a down clue, setting something up raises it, so the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: loci is the plural of locus, a place

explanation.surface: A military leader positions troops in an Indian city.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'set up' reads the places word from the bottom, and 'in' is the container signal; Agricola was Tacitus's father-in-law.
explanation.definitionFit: Gnaeus Julius Agricola was the Roman general who governed Britain and campaigned in Scotland.

clue.text: Flighty type gets round Yugoslav

parts.note: a tit is a small bird, a creature of flight
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A scatterbrain is turned round by a man from the Balkans.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty type' suggests a fickle person, but it is a bird that flies. TITO was Yugoslavia's post-war leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Josip Broz Tito led Yugoslavia from 1945 until his death in 1980.

clue.text: Guard against jab and belt him roughly

indicators.note: rough handling puts letters out of order, so these are to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Protect yourself from a punch and give the man a rough thrashing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jab' suggests a punch, but here it is a needle prick in sewing.
explanation.definitionFit: A thimble covers the fingertip so the sewing needle cannot prick it.

clue.text: After disturbed rest, oddly, night bird is to provide reinforcement

indicators.note: disturbed things are moved out of place, so these letters are jumbled
oddly picks the letters in odd positions, first, third and fifth

parts.note: a hen is a female bird

explanation.surface: After a broken sleep, an owl has to bolster its defences.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disturbed' scrambles the rest into STRE and 'oddly' works on 'night', not on 'rest'; the night bird looks like an owl but only the hen is a bird here.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen is to make stronger, which is to reinforce.

clue.text: Greek male embraces girl

indicators.note: to embrace is to hug, so the girl's name sits inside the male word

parts.note: he is the male pronoun
Ellen is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A man gives a woman a hug.
explanation.walkthrough: 'embraces' is the container signal; the Greeks call their land Hellas, hence the name.
explanation.definitionFit: A Hellene is a Greek, from Hellas, the Greeks' own name for their country.

clue.text: Careless southern Demo erat takes in Polish revolutionary

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it within, so the jumbled letters go between the two outer letters

parts.note: S is short for south or southern
D stands for Democrat in US politics

indicators.note: a revolution overturns things, so the word Polish is rearranged

explanation.surface: A slapdash Southern Democrat welcomes a radical from Poland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish revolutionary' reads as a radical from Poland; 'revolutionary' is the anagram signal giving LIPSHO, and 'takes in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Slipshod work is sloppy and done without due care.

clue.text: Way to hit and hit again

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for street, a way
to rap is to strike sharply

explanation.surface: A method of striking someone and then striking them again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'again' points to the second 'hit' as the definition, the first being the wordplay's RAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To strap someone is to beat them with a leather belt, giving repeated blows.

clue.text: His lessons include British, perhaps

indicators.note: words that include something contain it, here as a run of letters across the two words

explanation.surface: A teacher's classes cover Britain, for instance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'British, perhaps' is a definition by example: the British Isles are one such group.
explanation.definitionFit: The British group is one example of a cluster of islands, as are the Canary group.

clue.text: Cure, when off-colour

indicators.note: something off is spoilt or out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Feeling unwell, someone looks for a remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off-colour' means ill, but it splits into 'off', the anagram signal, and 'colour', the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ecru is the pale beige of unbleached linen, a shade of off-white.

clue.text: One, perhaps, surrenders opening to Italian monarch

indicators.note: giving up an opening means losing the first letter

parts.note: one is an example of a number

explanation.surface: Someone yields a vacancy to the king of Italy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'surrenders opening' drops the N from NUMBER, leaving UMBER. Umberto I and Umberto II were kings of Italy.
explanation.definitionFit: Umberto I and Umberto II were kings of Italy, the second reigning briefly in 1946.

clue.text: Cold house left English artist with illness

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
RA stands for Royal Academician, a member of Britain's Royal Academy of Arts

explanation.surface: A chilly home left an English painter sick.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Cholera is an acute bacterial infection of the intestine, a serious disease.

clue.text: In letters to St Paul, mistakenly gives strong advice

indicators.note: one piece in another sits inside it, so the jumble goes within the letters word

parts.note: exes is the plural of the letter X

indicators.note: a mistake puts things in the wrong order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: In his epistles to St Paul, someone wrongly offers forceful counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'letters' suggests epistles to St Paul, yet it is the plural of a letter of the alphabet; 'mistakenly' scrambles 'to St Paul' into POSTULAT and 'In' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To expostulate is to remonstrate or argue earnestly against something, urging another course.
